items.title: MiniMax indexes 11 community additions to its open H3 video and audio model
items.summary: MiniMax added 11 community projects to its H3 ecosystem index, including 8-step reference-conditioned video plus audio generation, a 4-step distillation, sparse attention, reference-token compression, and serving paths for GPUs, TPUs and Apple Silicon.

doubt.source: Roundup curated by the vendor; each linked project is community work that was not tested here.

items.title: tinygrad reports about 1000 tok/s aggregate decode for GLM-5.3-Flash on tinybox red flash
items.summary: tinygrad says its tinybox red flash now serves GLM-5.3-Flash at IQ4_XS with a full 262k context for a single user and about 1000 tok/s aggregate decode across many users, up from the 220 tok/s single-user figure it posted Oct 22. It says Terminal-Bench and DeepSWE runs are in progress.

doubt.source: Vendor's own numbers on its own hardware; concurrency level and benchmark method not stated.

items.title: Independent test runs Nanbeige4.3-33B as a coding agent on one A6000
items.summary: A tester ran Nanbeige4.3-33B (kept 2026-10-25) under vLLM 0.32 with FP8 weights and an NVFP4 KV cache on an Ampere A6000, getting a 113K-token cache pool at about 19 tok/s. In a coding-agent demo it fixed 5 of 5 planted bugs in a Dijkstra implementation and passed 8 of 8 hidden tests.

doubt.source: Single demo on a task the tester built; one run.

items.title: Hydro project releases Infinity, a Rust agent runtime that hibernates agents between tool calls
items.summary: Infinity is an Apache-2.0 Rust framework where an agent between turns is only its conversation history, so waiting agents cost no process and wake on the next event; the README claims 75k agents fit in a Raspberry Pi's memory. It includes a Reactive Agent Protocol that runs existing MCP servers through a compatibility layer, AWS Lambda deploy constructs, and a coding agent; sandbox crates v0.2.0 shipped Oct 22.

doubt.source: The 75k-agent figure is the project's own README claim; repo is young (27 stars).

security_forwarded.note: Pillar Security (disclosed 2026-10-19, THN https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/opencode-flaw-lets-malicious-mcp.html): opencode 1.0.137 to 1.18.32 passes a remote MCP server's OAuth authorization_endpoint to open@10, allowing PowerShell $(...) command injection on Windows/WSL when the user connects a malicious MCP server; fixed 1.18.33 (2026-09-28); no CVE, proposed CVSS 9.8; macOS/Linux not affected. Distinct from the OpenCode Console key breach. Related MCP Inspector GHSA-q978-78c7-phqw fixed in 2.12.0 (same fix line as the already-forwarded Inspector advisories). Box check: no opencode binary or global npm install; box is Linux.

security_forwarded.matched: Node.js (npm); always_forward: supply chain npm, agent tooling/MCP
security_forwarded.note: Elastic (REF8801, THN https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/fake-web3-accelerator-uses-npm-packages.html): fake Web3 accelerator lure ships npm packages @apexacc/cli and @apexacc/audit (an MCP server) that drop an infostealer/backdoor on Windows and macOS (CloudSyncD persistence), rewrite OPENROUTER_BASE_URL to arena.apexaccs.org to proxy LLM traffic, and register a rogue MCP server in ~/.apex/agent/mcp.json. Box check: no @apexacc packages, no ~/.apex, no apexaccs strings in ~/.config, ~/.cursor or ~/.claude, OPENROUTER_BASE_URL unset.
